I was a member when I was in college. There isn't really much to it. You can be as involved as you want. I didn't do much with it. They had a few functions and fundraisers occasionally. It is mostly just a resume builder.

I think there was a entry fee, but I can't remember how much it was at the time. There isn't really a downside to joining except that you will get "special" credit card and insurance offers in the mail for years after you graduate.

I had the opportunity to interact with the leadership of my college's Phi Theta Kappa branch a modest amount in my time at community college. I'll try to share what I can without revealing too much personally identifiable information.

So first off, lets get down to what PTK presents itself as. PTK is referred to as an "honor society", which is a fraternal organization, which is a club where people help each other out, where they ostensibly only pick smart/useful people for membership.

Fraternal organizations are not a new thing. They have existed for a long time. The Masons, the Skull and Bones, the Rotary Club, The Rosicrucians, Lions Club, etc. These are all fraternal orgazations who accept members, and their main obligation is to help their fellow members out. Fraternal orgazations like PTK, phit beta kappa (PTK's parent organzation), Skull and Bones, Scroll and Key, etc. are used to identify useful people, to give them a leg up over everyone else, to develop networking and to gain leverage over those who you help so they can help you when you need it.

PTK is a branch of Phi Beta Kappa. Phi Beta Kappa itself is very closely related to freemasonry, and they both share some odd rituals and weird symbols with freemasonry. I don't really know what that is all about, but it always struck me as a bit odd. I don't have a problem with freemasonry, but there is a verifiable link to it that one should be aware of.

Now, most people who join PTK do it for the scholarships. Join PTK and very often you get free money for college. That's how they attract a lot of people. My impression is that most people just do it for the free money, and then forget about being a member.

So ok, thats some background stuff. My experiences interacting with the leadership in my local PTK group. These are people without scruples or morals. It is entirely about what you can get away with in a self-serving way. The faculty sponsor for the group was embezzling money, but those with evidence were encouraged to stay quiet about it. The president of the group was a backstabbing bitch. And they actively tried to sabotage the formation of a student government organization on campus which threatened to disrupt the stranglehold they had on what the administration of the college did.

So PTK itself might not be bad. You can join and be a good person, get free money, and that's it. But it does lend itself toward corrupt behavior in my experience. Just be wary if people attempt to coerce you into doing something for the group or for fellow members because you owe them for helping you out.
